description:
Publish a post: put it live on the site under /content and, if it has email enabled with a list, email it to every active subscriber on that list. Publishing a post that is already published, or that was emailed before and has since been unpublished, re-sends the email to the whole list. Same as `micropage posts publish <slug>`.

Needs the confirmation_token from preview_post_send, taken after the post's last change; show the user that preview and get their go-ahead first. A stale or missing token is refused with nothing changed.

Posts that would send email are refused unless the user has set MICROPAGE_MCP_ALLOW_SEND=1 in this server's config; there is no web-only override, so to publish such a post on the web only, save it with email: false first. When the client supports it the user is also asked to confirm the send directly. The site rebuild redeploys the live build, so an unpublished page draft left by save_page or the editor stays a draft. It returns build_id and after_event_id to follow the rebuild with get_deploy_status. Use unpublish_post to take a post down.

confirmation_token.description: The confirmation_token from preview_post_send for this post, taken after its last change and shown to the user.

project.description: Which project: its uuid, its numeric id, its micropage hostname ("acme" or "acme.micropage.sh") or its custom domain ("www.acme.com"). A full URL also works. Get valid values from list_projects.

slug.description: The post's slug, as list_posts shows it (e.g. "launching-new-dashboard"). Normalised like the CLI does.

name: publish_post

after_event_id.description: Pass to get_deploy_status with build_id to see only events from this rebuild.

build_id.description: The build the site rebuild redeploys: the live one, not an unpublished page draft. Pass to get_deploy_status; null when nothing was rebuilt.

rebuild_queued.description: True when a site rebuild was queued so the post appears under /content.

title: Publish a micropage post (may send email)
